title: VELARIUM dev update: six characters, five evolution stages, and a lot more animation work than I expected
author: Competitive_Might709
selftext:
Hey everyone! I wanted to share some progress on VELARIUM, an action game I’m developing in Godot 4.

I’ve been working on a development version called V-Next, focusing on the characters, weapons and interface. The game has six characters: Knight, Ronin, Wizard, Witch, ZAD and MECHA, with five evolution stages each. I’ve been working on character selection, the upgrade area, the Forge, the Rift Gate and other menus. Character effects have also been added, which is starting to give the game more personality.

The part that turned out to be much harder than I expected was getting everything to work together. For example, I discovered that some models downloaded in a batch came without bones, so they had to be exported again with rigs. Then came the other problems: capes deforming, stances that don’t suit the character, hands clipping through weapons or not really gripping them, and animations changing unexpectedly when switching weapons.

There have been some targeted improvements: Ronin’s grip, conflicting animation ownership on Knight, carry adjustments for MECHA, and fixes for some staff grips. These don’t solve every combination, and they haven’t all been verified in a full gameplay test. ZAD has an experimental rifle-grip solution that has been tested separately, but it isn’t integrated into the game yet.

What I want to tackle next is making each character feel unique in motion, not just in appearance: their idle, walk, run, weapon grip and transitions. I’m also investigating FPS drops and performance. I’d rather share the process honestly than call something finished before it actually works.

If you’ve worked with rigged characters and separate weapons in Godot, how did you approach matching the hands, weapon and animations? I’d also love to hear what you think of the overall direction.
